statement: The linear–quadratic regulator (LQR) is an optimal state-feedback controller for a linear dynamical system governed by linear differential equations (continuous-time) or linear difference equations (discrete-time) that minimizes a quadratic cost function. For continuous-time finite-horizon systems \dot{\mathbf{x}} = A\mathbf{x} + B\mathbf{u} with quadratic cost J = \mathbf{x}^{\mathsf{T}}(t_1)F(t_1)\mathbf{x}(t_1) + \int_{t_0}^{t_1} (\mathbf{x}^{\mathsf{T}}Q\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{u}^{\mathsf{T}}R\mathbf{u} + 2\mathbf{x}^{\mathsf{T}}N\mathbf{u})\,dt, the feedback control law is given by \mathbf{u} = -K\mathbf{x}, where K = R^{-1}(B^{\mathsf{T}}P(t) + N^{\mathsf{T}}), and P(t) satisfies the continuous-time Riccati differential equation A^{\mathsf{T}}P(t) + P(t)A - [P(t)B + N]R^{-1}[B^{\mathsf{T}}P(t) + N^{\mathsf{T}}] + Q = -\dot{P}(t) with boundary condition P(t_1) = F(t_1). The supplied source contains no derivation of these equations (e.g., via dynamic programming, completing the square, or solving the first-order conditions), but only provides the definitions, problem formulations, and resulting equations.

symbols.meaning: cross-term (state and control) cost weighting matrix
co-state vector in first-order necessary conditions
discrete-time feedback gain matrix at time step k
discrete-time Riccati matrix at time step k

properties.property: Inherent robustness with guaranteed gain and phase margins
properties.why: LQR controllers possess guaranteed stability margins as an inherent property in optimal control theory
LQR provides the optimal state feedback law used in the complete solution to the LQG problem

properties.property: Stationary algebraic Riccati equation (CARE) in infinite-horizon continuous time
properties.why: The time derivative of P vanishes as the horizon approaches infinity, yielding A^{\mathsf{T}}P + PA - (PB + N)R^{-1}(B^{\mathsf{T}}P + N^{\mathsf{T}}) + Q = 0

properties.property: Backward-in-time iteration of the dynamic Riccati equation in finite-horizon discrete time
properties.why: P_{k-1} is computed recursively from the terminal condition P_{H_p} = Q_{H_p} using P_{k-1} = A^{\mathsf{T}}P_k A - (A^{\mathsf{T}}P_k B + N)(R + B^{\mathsf{T}}P_k B)^{-1}(B^{\mathsf{T}}P_k A + N^{\mathsf{T}}) + Q

properties.property: Discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation (DARE) solvability via dynamic iteration
properties.why: The unique positive definite solution to the DARE can be obtained by iterating the discrete-time dynamic Riccati equation until convergence

properties.property: Equivalence to model predictive control (MPC) under receding horizon and linear constraints
properties.why: Solving finite-horizon LQR repeatedly with a receding horizon under constraints C\mathbf{x} + D\mathbf{u} \le \mathbf{e}$ constitutes convex MPC

assumptions.assumption: System dynamics are strictly linear differential or difference equations
assumptions.breaks_when: System dynamics are nonlinear, quadratic (QQR), or polynomial (PQR)

assumptions.assumption: Cost function is strictly quadratic in state and control vectors
assumptions.breaks_when: Non-quadratic cost criteria, non-convex penalties, or asymmetric performance specifications are used

assumptions.assumption: Control weighting matrix R (or R + B^{\mathsf{T}}P_{k+1}B in discrete-time) is invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: Control effort is unpenalized or R is singular / rank-deficient

assumptions.assumption: Full state vector \mathbf{x} is directly measurable and available for feedback
assumptions.breaks_when: State is only partially observed through noisy output measurements, requiring an observer or Kalman filter (LQG)

assumptions.assumption: Unconstrained state and control spaces in the standard Riccati synthesis
assumptions.breaks_when: Physical actuator saturation or state constraints C\mathbf{x} + D\mathbf{u} \le \mathbf{e} become active

failure_modes.mode: Singular control weighting matrix inversion failure
failure_modes.signature: Computation of gain matrix K or discrete Riccati step halts or produces numerical overflow
failure_modes.cause: R or (R + B^{\mathsf{T}}P B) is singular or ill-conditioned

failure_modes.mode: Suboptimal or unacceptable closed-loop dynamic behavior
failure_modes.signature: Closed-loop system fails to meet desired transient or tracking design goals despite minimizing J
failure_modes.cause: Difficulty in identifying and tuning appropriate weighting matrices Q, R, and N that reflect true operational specifications

failure_modes.signature: Real system exceeds allowable control authority or safety boundaries C\mathbf{x} + D\mathbf{u} \le \mathbf{e}
failure_modes.cause: Standard LQR feedback control law \mathbf{u} = -K\mathbf{x} assumes unconstrained operation
